questions.a: Laying boards across the puddles and dumping extra dirt on the path.

questions.q: What was the real cause of the muddy path?
questions.a: It was the lowest part of the garden, so rain from every plot ran there with nowhere to go.

questions.q: How did the ditch and rain barrels solve the problem?
questions.a: The gravel ditch carried water away from the path, and the barrels caught rain from the roof.

sessions.title: The Blinking Plant Reminder
paragraphs: Priya was in charge of watering the plants in her family's apartment, but she kept forgetting. Every few days, she would notice the fern by the window drooping. Its leaves were turning brown and crunchy at the edges. Her parents reminded her, but soon everyone forgot. Priya wanted to solve the problem.

First, she tried writing a note that said Water the Plants and sticking it on the fridge. For two days it worked, but then the note got covered by school papers. Next, she tried setting an alarm on her mom's phone. The alarm went off while Priya was at soccer practice. By the time she got home, she had forgotten all about it.

Priya thought about why the reminders were failing. The note was easy to ignore, and the alarm rang at the wrong time and place. She needed a reminder that would show up right when the plant needed water, in a spot where she would see it. Then she remembered the sensor in her science kit, a tool that can tell when soil is dry.

Priya decided to invent her own plant reminder. With help from her uncle, she hooked the sensor up to a small battery and a bright green light. She pushed the sensor into the fern's pot and set the light on a shelf by her bedroom door. When the soil got dry, the light would blink, and she passed that door every morning.

Three days later, Priya woke up and saw the green light blinking. She gave the fern a long drink, and the light turned off. Over the next month, the fern grew bright new leaves. Finally, her problem was solved. Priya learned that the best fix is often one that fits the way people really live.

stops.question: What problem does Priya's family have?
stops.lookFor: Priya keeps forgetting to water the plants, so the fern is drooping and turning brown.

stops.question: Why didn't the note or the phone alarm work?
stops.lookFor: The note got covered up, and the alarm rang when Priya was not home, so she forgot again.

stops.lookFor: One that shows up right when the plant needs water and right where she will see it.

questions.a: A note on the refrigerator and an alarm on her mother's phone.

questions.a: A moisture sensor connected to a green light that blinks by her bedroom door when the soil is dry.

questions.a: It reminded her at the right time, when the soil was dry, and in a place she passed every morning.

sessions.title: Two Clocks, One Call
paragraphs: Kofi and Sam had been best friends since kindergarten. When Sam's family moved to England, both boys promised to talk every week. Their first video call did not go well. Kofi called right after school, but in England it was already late in the evening, and Sam had gone to bed. The problem was that England is five hours ahead of Kofi's town.

The boys tried to fix it in a few ways. First, Kofi tried calling before school, but that was the middle of Sam's school day, and phones were not allowed in class. Next, Sam tried staying up late on a school night to wait for the call. He was so sleepy that he kept yawning, and his mom said they could not do that again.

Kofi felt frustrated, so he asked his older cousin for advice. She worked with people in other countries, and she showed him a chart with two clocks side by side. She said the trick was to find the hours when both people were awake and free. Kofi realized that they had been guessing instead of checking both clocks.

Kofi and Sam decided to make their own chart. They wrote down every hour of the weekend for both places. Then they crossed out the times when either of them was asleep, eating, or busy with sports. Only a few hours were left. On Saturday, ten in the morning for Kofi was three in the afternoon for Sam.

That Saturday, Kofi sat down with his breakfast and called. Sam answered right away, wide awake and smiling. They talked for an hour about school, soccer, and the rainy weather in England. Finally, the problem was solved. Kofi learned that a good plan works best when it fits everyone, not just you.

stops.question: What problem do Kofi and Sam have?
stops.lookFor: England is five hours ahead, so when Kofi calls after school, Sam is already asleep.

stops.question: Why didn't calling before school or staying up late work?
stops.lookFor: Before school was during Sam's school day, and staying up late made Sam too tired and was not allowed again.

stops.question: What did Kofi learn from his cousin that could help?
stops.lookFor: Use a chart with both clocks to find the hours when both people are awake and free, instead of guessing.

questions.q: What two tries did the boys make that did not work?
questions.a: Kofi calling before school, and Sam staying up late on a school night.

questions.q: What tool helped them find a solution?
questions.a: A chart showing the hours in both places side by side.

questions.q: How was the problem solved?
questions.a: They found a time that worked for both, Saturday at ten in the morning for Kofi and three in the afternoon for Sam.

sessions.title: Stars Behind the Streetlights
paragraphs: For her birthday, Grace got a small telescope. She could hardly wait to see the stars from her science book. That night she set it up in the backyard with her little brother, Noah. But when she looked through the eyepiece, she saw only a few faint dots and a hazy orange glow. She could barely see any stars.

First, Grace tried waiting for a clearer night, since she thought clouds were hiding the sky. Three nights later the weather was clear, yet the sky still looked dull and washed out. Next, she carried the telescope up to the highest window in the house. But the view was just as dim, and now she had to look past the neighbor's porch light.

Grace decided to ask a librarian. The librarian gave her a book about the night sky. In it, Grace read about light pollution, which happens when light from streetlights and buildings spreads into the sky. That glow hides faint stars, the way a flashlight is hard to notice on a sunny day. Her telescope worked fine, and the trouble was her neighborhood.

She asked her parents if they could visit a darker place. They found a state park about an hour away that welcomed stargazers. The family chose a night with no moon, since a bright moon can wash out the sky too. Grace packed a red flashlight, because red light protects your night vision better than white light.

When they arrived, the sky looked as if someone had spilled sugar across a black tablecloth. Through the telescope, Grace and Noah could see the planet Jupiter with four tiny moons beside it. Finally, the problem was solved. Grace learned that sometimes a problem is not in your tools, but in the place where you use them.

stops.question: What problem does Grace have with her new telescope?
stops.lookFor: She can barely see any stars, only a few faint dots and a hazy orange glow.

stops.question: Why didn't waiting for a clear night or moving higher up work?
stops.lookFor: Clouds and height were not the real cause; something else was making the sky bright and washed out.

stops.question: What did Grace learn from the book, and how does it point to a solution?
stops.lookFor: Light pollution from streetlights and buildings hides faint stars, so she needs to go somewhere darker.

questions.a: Waiting for a clear night and moving the telescope to the highest window.

questions.q: What was the real cause of the problem?
questions.a: Light pollution from streetlights, signs, and buildings in her neighborhood.

questions.q: How did Grace finally solve the problem?
questions.a: Her family took the telescope to a dark state park on a moonless night.

sessions.title: The Bread That Would Not Rise
paragraphs: Leah wanted to surprise her family by baking homemade bread for Sunday dinner. She followed a recipe from her grandfather's old cookbook, mixing flour, water, salt, and yeast into a sticky dough. The recipe said the dough should rest for an hour and double in size. But an hour later, the dough looked the same, flat and heavy in the bowl.

Leah had a problem to figure out. First, she tried waiting another hour, thinking the dough might just need more time. Nothing changed. Then she tried kneading in more flour, because she guessed the dough was too wet to rise. The extra flour only made the dough stiff and dry, and it still refused to grow.

Leah called her grandfather, who asked how old the yeast was and how hot the water had been. The yeast had expired months ago, and she had used very hot tap water. He explained that yeast is a tiny living thing that makes bubbles of gas, and those bubbles make bread rise. Old yeast may be too weak, and very hot water can harm it.

Leah decided to start over with a fresh packet of yeast. This time she used water that felt warm on her wrist, like a bath, not like hot cocoa. She stirred in a spoonful of sugar to feed the yeast and waited ten minutes. Soon the mixture became foamy and smelled like bread, so the yeast was alive.

She mixed the dough again and set the bowl in a warm spot near the oven. An hour later, the dough had puffed up over the rim. Finally, the problem was solved, and the family cheered for her golden loaf at dinner. Leah learned that knowing why a recipe works can help you fix it when something goes wrong.

stops.question: What problem does Leah have with her bread?
stops.lookFor: The dough did not rise at all after resting for an hour.

stops.question: Why didn't waiting longer or adding flour fix the dough?
stops.lookFor: Neither one fixed the real cause; the dough was not missing time or flour, and the extra flour made it stiff.

stops.question: What did Leah learn from her grandfather that explains the problem?
stops.lookFor: Yeast is alive and makes the gas bubbles; her yeast was old and the hot water could have harmed it.

questions.q: What two things did Leah try that did not work?
questions.a: Waiting another hour and kneading in more flour.

questions.q: What were the real causes of the problem?
questions.a: The yeast had expired, and the water she used was too hot.

questions.q: How did Leah check that her new yeast was working before baking?
questions.a: She mixed it with warm water and sugar, and it became foamy and smelled like bread.

sessions.title: The Echoing Gym
paragraphs: Diego's school choir was getting ready for its spring concert, which would be held in the gym. During their first practice there, something strange happened. The singers on one side could not hear the singers on the other side. Every note seemed to bounce around the room, so the song turned into a blurry mess, and the choir kept falling out of time.

The choir tried more than one way to fix the problem. First, their director, Miss June, asked everyone to sing louder to cut through the noise. But the echo grew even stronger, and the song sounded like shouting. Next, she spread the singers out across the whole floor. That made it worse, because now the singers on the ends could not hear each other.

Diego remembered a science lesson about sound, and he raised his hand. He said that sound bounces off hard, flat things like walls, floors, and metal bleachers, the way a ball bounces off a wall. The gym had almost nothing soft to soak up the sound, so every note kept bouncing back. The choir did not need more volume; they needed less echo.

The choir decided to test his idea. Students brought in old blankets, and the custodian helped them hang the blankets along the back wall. They also placed soft gym mats on the floor in front of the bleachers. Then Miss June moved the choir into a tight half circle so the singers could hear one another.

When they sang the first song again, the notes sounded clear and smooth, and everyone stayed together. Finally, the problem was solved, and on the night of the concert, the audience could hear every word. Diego learned that science can help solve problems in places you would not expect, even in music.

stops.question: What is the problem the choir runs into in the gym?
stops.lookFor: The sound echoes, the singers cannot hear each other, and the song turns into a blurry mess.

stops.question: Why did singing louder and spreading out make things worse?
stops.lookFor: Louder singing made more echo, and spreading out put singers too far apart to hear each other.

stops.question: What did Diego understand about the problem that the others missed?
stops.lookFor: Sound bounces off hard surfaces, so they needed soft things to soak up the sound, not more volume.

questions.q: What two tries made the problem worse?
questions.a: Singing louder and spreading the singers across the whole floor.

questions.q: What was causing the echo?
questions.a: Sound bouncing off the gym's hard walls, floors, and metal bleachers with nothing soft to absorb it.

questions.q: How did the choir solve the problem?
questions.a: They hung blankets, put mats on the floor, and stood close together in a half circle.

sessions.title: Frogs and Toads
paragraphs: Frogs and toads look a lot alike. Both are small animals that can hop, and both start life as eggs in the water. The eggs hatch into tadpoles. A tadpole has a tail and swims like a fish. In time it grows legs, and then its tail goes away.

Frogs and toads eat the same kinds of food, and they both like bugs. They catch bugs with long, sticky tongues. The tongue shoots out fast and snaps back with a fly or a worm. Both of them help us, since they eat the bugs that bug us!

But frogs and toads are not the same. Look at their skin. Most frogs have smooth, wet skin, and most toads have dry skin with lots of bumps. A frog feels slick, but a toad feels rough. That is one way to tell them apart.
Their legs are different, too. Frogs have long back legs, so they can jump far in one big leap. Toads have short back legs, and they take small hops. Some of the time, a toad will just walk.
Frogs and toads live in different spots. Most frogs stay near a pond or a stream, since they need to keep their skin wet. Toads can live on dry land. You might see a toad in a yard, far from a pond.

So frogs and toads are alike in some ways. They both hop, they both eat bugs, and they both start as tadpoles. However, their skin, their legs, and their homes are different. Next time you see one, look close. Can you tell which it is?

stops.question: Is this part telling how frogs and toads are the same or how they are different? How do you know?
stops.lookFor: Same; the words 'same' and 'both' show they eat bugs and catch them the same way.

stops.question: What word at the start of this part tells you the author is switching to something new?
stops.lookFor: 'But' tells us the author is now showing a difference (their skin).

stops.question: Why do you think the author keeps putting frogs and toads side by side in each part?
stops.lookFor: So we can see each way they match or don't match, one thing at a time, like legs, skin, or homes.

questions.q: Name one way frogs and toads are alike.
questions.a: Both hop, eat bugs with sticky tongues, or start life as tadpoles.

questions.q: Name one way frogs and toads are different.
questions.a: Frogs have smooth, wet skin and long legs; toads have dry, bumpy skin and short legs.

questions.q: Which clue words in the story helped you know when the author was showing a difference?
questions.a: Words like 'but,' 'different,' 'however,' and 'not the same.'

sessions.title: Cats and Dogs
paragraphs: Cats and dogs are pets in lots of homes, and they are alike in many ways. Both have fur, four legs, and a tail. Both like to play. And both need food, water, and care from the people who love them.
Cats and dogs both have a good nose, and they can smell things that we can not. They both hear well, too. A cat or a dog can hear a sound that is much too soft for you to hear.

But cats and dogs act in different ways. Most dogs like to be with a group, and they want to be near their people all day. Lots of cats like to be on their own. A cat may sit with you for a while, and then it will walk off to nap.
They do not play the same way. A dog may run to get a ball and bring it back to you. A cat likes to hunt a toy. It hides and waits, and then it jumps! A cat can climb up high, but most dogs can not.
Cats and dogs talk in different ways, too. A dog barks to say hi, and it barks if a stranger is near. A cat meows. When a cat is glad, it may purr. When a dog is glad, it wags its tail.
So cats and dogs are alike, but they are not the same. Both make good pets, and both need love and care. Which one would you like to have in your home?

stops.question: Is this part showing how cats and dogs are alike or different? What word gave you a clue?
stops.lookFor: Alike; the word 'both' shows they both smell and hear well.

stops.question: The author just switched from alike to different. What word told you?
stops.lookFor: 'But' and 'different' show the author is now telling how they act in different ways.

stops.question: How does the author show the difference in how cats and dogs play?
stops.lookFor: The author tells what a dog does (gets a ball) and then what a cat does (hides and jumps), side by side.

questions.q: How are cats and dogs alike?
questions.a: Both have fur, four legs, and a tail; both like to play, smell and hear well, and need care.

questions.q: How are cats and dogs different?
questions.a: Dogs like to be with people more, fetch balls, and bark; cats like time alone, hunt toys, climb, and meow or purr.

questions.q: Why did the author write about cats and dogs together?
questions.a: They are both common pets, so comparing them helps us see what is the same and what is special about each.

sessions.title: Rain and Snow
paragraphs: Rain and snow both fall from the sky, and they both come from clouds. A cloud is made of tiny drops of water or bits of ice. When the drops or bits get big, they get heavy. Then they fall down to the ground.
Rain and snow are both made of water, so that is the same. Both help plants grow, and both fill up ponds, lakes, and rivers. We need them both to live. The water we drink comes from rain and snow.
But rain and snow are not alike in all ways. Rain falls as wet drops, but snow is made of ice. It falls in soft, white flakes. Most flakes have six sides, and no two flakes look just the same.

The big difference is how cold it is. Rain falls when the air is warm. Snow falls when the air is cold, and it must be cold enough to make ice. Then the water in the cloud will freeze, and it falls as snow.

Rain and snow feel different, too. Rain splashes on the ground and makes puddles that you can jump in. Snow piles up on the ground, and it is soft and cold. You can make a snowman with snow, but you can not make one with rain!
So rain and snow are alike, since they are both water from clouds. However, rain is wet drops and snow is ice. Which do you like to play in more, rain or snow? Why do you like it best?

stops.question: Is this part telling how rain and snow are alike or different? How can you tell?
stops.lookFor: Alike; the author uses 'both' and 'the same' to show they are both water that helps plants and fills lakes.

stops.question: What clue words in this part show a difference?
stops.lookFor: 'The big difference' and comparing 'warm' with 'cold' show how rain and snow are not the same.

stops.question: Why do you think the author compared rain and snow instead of just telling about one?
stops.lookFor: They both fall from clouds, so comparing them helps us see why they turn out different, like warm versus cold air.

questions.q: How are rain and snow the same?
questions.a: Both come from clouds, are made of water, and help plants grow.

questions.q: What is the big difference between rain and snow?
questions.a: Rain falls when the air is warm; snow falls when it is cold enough for water to freeze into ice.

questions.q: What word does the author use at the end to show a difference is coming?
questions.a: 'However.'

sessions.title: Soccer and Basketball
paragraphs: Soccer and basketball are two of the most popular sports in the world. Kids play them at school, in parks, and on teams. The two games are alike in some big ways. But they are also very different.

First, let's look at how they are the same. Both games are played by two teams. Each team tries to score by getting a ball into a goal. In both sports, players must pass the ball and work together. One player can not win the game alone.

Both games also take a lot of running. Players dash up and down the field or the court. They need strong legs and lots of breath. That is why soccer and basketball players are some of the fittest athletes around.

However, the way players move the ball is different. In soccer, players kick the ball with their feet. They can bump it with their heads, too. Most of the time, only the goalie may use hands. In basketball, players use their hands. They bounce the ball as they move, and they shoot it at a hoop.

The places they play are not the same, either. Soccer is played on a big field of grass. A basketball court is much smaller, and it is often inside a gym. A soccer goal sits on the ground. A basketball hoop hangs ten feet off the floor.

The scores are different, too. Soccer games often end with just a few goals. In basketball, a shot can be worth one, two, or three points. So scores get high fast. Unlike soccer, a basketball game can end with a score like 80 to 75.

stops.question: Is this part about how the sports are alike or different? What words helped you know?
stops.lookFor: Alike; 'the same,' 'both,' and 'each team' show both sports have teams, goals, and passing.

stops.question: The author started this part with 'However.' What does that word tell you?
stops.lookFor: It signals a switch from how they are alike to how they are different, starting with how the ball is moved.

sessions.title: Bees and Wasps
paragraphs: Bees and wasps are both insects that buzz and fly. People often mix them up. They look alike at first, and both can sting. But if you look closely, you will see that they are not the same.

Bees and wasps have the same basic body plan. Both have six legs, four wings, and three body parts. Lots of them have yellow and black stripes. Some bees and some wasps live in big groups with a queen in charge of laying eggs.

Their bodies are different in other ways, though. A honeybee is round and fuzzy. Its hair helps it carry pollen from flower to flower. A wasp is smooth and shiny. It has a thin waist, like a narrow belt between its middle and its back end.

Bees and wasps also eat different foods. Bees drink nectar from flowers and eat pollen. Wasps sip some nectar too. But lots of wasps also hunt other insects. They feed these bugs to their young. This helps keep garden pests away.

Their homes are not alike, either. Honeybees build combs out of wax that they make in their own bodies. They store honey in the combs. Lots of wasps make paper nests. They chew wood into a soft paste and shape it into rooms.

So bees and wasps are alike in some ways. Both buzz, both fly, and both help nature. However, bees are fuzzy flower helpers, while lots of wasps are smooth bug hunters. Both are best watched from a safe distance!

sessions.title: The Sun and the Moon
paragraphs: The Sun and the Moon are the two biggest lights in our sky. We see the Sun by day, and we often see the Moon at night. From Earth, they look about the same size. But they are very different.

The Sun and the Moon are alike in a few ways. Both look round, and both seem to rise in the east and set in the west. That is because Earth spins. As it turns, the Sun and the Moon both seem to move across the sky.

However, the Sun and the Moon are not the same kind of thing. The Sun is a star, a giant ball of hot gas that makes its own light. The Moon is made of rock, and it does not make any light at all. It shines because sunlight bounces off it.

Their sizes are very different. The Sun is huge, and more than one million Earths could fit inside it! The Moon is much smaller than Earth. It only looks as big as the Sun because it is so much closer to us.
They also move in different ways. The Moon travels around Earth, and it takes about a month to go all the way around. Earth travels around the Sun, and that trip takes one whole year.

The Sun and the Moon look like partners in the sky, since both are round and both move across it each day. But one is a blazing star, and the other is a rocky ball. Never look right at the Sun. Just think about how different they really are!

sessions.title: Alligators and Crocodiles
paragraphs: Alligators and crocodiles are two of the largest reptiles on Earth. Many people call them gators and crocs for short. They look so much alike that lots of people can not tell them apart. Still, if you know what to look for, you can spot the differences.

These two animals share many features. Both have long bodies covered in tough, scaly skin. Both have strong tails that help them swim. Their eyes and noses sit on top of their heads, so they can float low in the water and still see and breathe.

Gators and crocs also live in the same kinds of ways. Both lay eggs in nests on land. Both are hunters that wait without a sound for fish, birds, and other animals to come close. Both lie in the sun to warm up their bodies.

The best way to tell them apart is the snout. A gator has a wide, round snout shaped like the letter U. A croc has a long, thin snout shaped more like a V. When a croc shuts its mouth, you can still see some of its bottom teeth. A gator's bottom teeth mostly hide.

They also live in different places. Gators live mostly in fresh water, like swamps and rivers. They are found in the United States and China. Crocs can live in salty water, too. They are found in many warm parts of the world.

In the end, gators and crocs are alike in their bodies and the way they hunt. However, their snouts, teeth, and homes are different. The southern tip of Florida is the only place on Earth where both live in the wild side by side.

sessions.title: Rivers and Lakes
paragraphs: Rivers and lakes are both bodies of water. Most of them hold fresh water, not salt water like the ocean. You might swim, fish, or ride a boat on either one. They seem alike, but each one has its own shape and story.
In some ways, rivers and lakes are the same. Both get their water from rain and melting snow. Both are homes for fish, frogs, turtles, and plants. People and animals use both for drinking water, too.

The biggest difference is that a river moves. River water flows downhill, from a high place to a lower one. Most rivers end when they reach a lake, a bigger river, or the ocean. Lake water mostly stays in one place. It sits in a low spot in the land, like water in a bowl.

Because of this, rivers and lakes have different shapes. A river is long and thin, like a ribbon. It can twist and bend for hundreds of miles. A lake is wider and rounder. It has a shore all the way around it.

Rivers and lakes also change the land in different ways. Moving river water carries sand and small rocks with it. Over a very long time, a river can carve a deep valley or even a canyon. A lake is calmer. Its still water lets mud settle slowly to the bottom.

Rivers and lakes are often linked. A river may flow into a lake, and another river may flow out of it. So the two work like partners. Both give life to plants and animals. But one is always on the move, while the other stays still.

sessions.title: Dolphins and Sharks
paragraphs: Dolphins and sharks both swim in the ocean. From far away, they can look a lot alike. Both have smooth gray bodies with a fin on their backs. However, these two animals belong to very different groups.

Let's start with how they are alike. Both dolphins and sharks are fast, strong swimmers. Their bodies are long and pointed at the front, which helps them slide through the water. Both are hunters that eat fish and other sea animals.

The biggest difference is what kind of animal each one is. A shark is a fish. It breathes by taking oxygen from the water with its gills. A dolphin is a mammal, just like you. It has lungs and must swim to the top to breathe air through a blowhole.
They also swim in different ways. A shark moves its tail from side to side. A dolphin moves its tail up and down. If you watch closely, this is one way to tell them apart in the water.

Their babies are different, too. Dolphin mothers give birth to live babies called calves. The mother feeds her calf milk and stays close to it for a long time. Many sharks also have live babies, but some lay eggs. Shark babies, called pups, swim off on their own right away.
So dolphins and sharks share the same ocean home, and they have similar shapes. Yet one is a fish with gills, and the other is a mammal with lungs. Both are amazing animals of the sea.

sessions.title: T. rex and Triceratops
paragraphs: Tyrannosaurus rex and Triceratops are two of the most famous dinosaurs ever found. They lived at the same time, near the end of the age of dinosaurs, in what is now western North America. Scientists have learned about both of them by studying their fossil bones.

These two dinosaurs had a lot in common. Both were huge animals that weighed several tons, about as much as an elephant or more. Both hatched from eggs. Both had strong legs and thick tails. Each one was among the biggest creatures in its world.

However, they ate very different food. T. rex was a meat eater with huge jaws full of sharp teeth as long as bananas. Triceratops was a plant eater. It used a hard beak, like a parrot's, to snip tough plants, and rows of teeth in the back to slice them up.

Their bodies were built differently, too. T. rex walked on two powerful back legs. Its front arms were tiny, and they were too short to reach its mouth. Triceratops walked on all four legs, a bit like a giant rhino. Its body was low and wide.

The most famous difference is on their heads. Triceratops had three horns, with one on its nose and two long ones above its eyes. Behind its head was a large bony frill, like a shield. T. rex had no horns or frill at all. Its greatest tool was its mighty bite.

Scientists have found Triceratops bones with T. rex tooth marks on them. So these two giants really did cross paths. They shared the same land and the same time. But one was a hunter with sharp teeth, and the other was a plant eater with horns.

sessions.title: Earth and Mars
paragraphs: Earth and Mars are neighbors in our solar system. Earth is the third planet from the Sun, and Mars is the fourth. Scientists study Mars closely because, in some ways, it is a lot like our home planet.

Both Earth and Mars are rocky planets. You could stand on either one, unlike giant gas planets such as Jupiter. Both have mountains, valleys, and volcanoes. Both have ice caps at their north and south poles. A day on Mars is just a little longer than a day on Earth.

Even so, the two planets are very different. Earth is almost twice as wide as Mars. Mars is farther from the Sun, so it is much colder. On a normal day, Mars is colder than the coldest winter night in most places on Earth.

The air is different, too. Earth has thick air that we can breathe. Mars has very thin air made mostly of a gas called carbon dioxide. People can not breathe it. A person on Mars would need a space suit and a supply of air.

Water may be the biggest difference of all. Oceans cover most of Earth, and its rivers and lakes are full of life. Mars is a dry, dusty desert. Its red color comes from rusty dust on the ground. Scientists think Mars had rivers and lakes long ago, but today its water is mostly frozen.

Robot rovers have been rolling across Mars for years to learn more. They help us compare the two planets. By studying how Mars and Earth are alike and different, scientists hope to learn if tiny living things ever existed on the Red Planet.

sessions.title: Pianos and Guitars
paragraphs: The piano and the guitar are two of the most popular instruments in the world. People play them in homes, schools, and concert halls. Both can play a song all by themselves, or they can join a whole band.

These two instruments make sound in a similar way. Both have strings. When a string moves back and forth very fast, it makes a sound. Thin, short strings make high notes, and thick, long strings make low notes. Both can play many notes at once, which is called a chord.

However, players make the strings move in different ways. On a guitar, you pluck or strum the strings with your fingers or a small pick. On a piano, you never touch the strings at all. Instead, you press keys. Each key moves a small felt hammer that taps a string inside.

Their size is another big difference. A guitar is light enough to carry on your back to a friend's house or a campfire. A piano is large and heavy, so it usually stays in one room. Moving a piano can take several strong people.

The number of notes is also different. A regular piano has 88 keys, so it can play a wide range of sounds, from deep rumbles to tiny high tinkles. A regular guitar has only six strings. Players press the strings down along the neck to change the notes.
Many musicians learn to play both. Each one helps you learn about notes, rhythm, and chords. Whether you choose the piano or the guitar, practice is the key to making beautiful music.

sessions.title: Hurricanes and Tornadoes
paragraphs: Hurricanes and tornadoes are two of the strongest kinds of storms on Earth. People sometimes mix them up because both have fast, spinning winds. However, these storms start in their own places, grow to their own sizes, and last for very different lengths of time.

First, let's look at how they are alike. Both storms are made of air that spins around a center. Both form when warm, wet air rises into the sky. For both kinds of storms, weather experts watch closely and warn people so they can stay safe.

The biggest difference is size. A hurricane is huge. It can be hundreds of miles wide. From space, it looks like a giant swirl of clouds with a calm hole in the middle, called the eye. A tornado is much smaller. Most are less than a mile across, and each one reaches down from a single storm cloud.

They also form in different places. A hurricane begins over warm ocean water near the equator, and the warm sea gives the storm its strength. Tornadoes most often form over land. The United States has more tornadoes than any other country, and many of them strike in spring.

Time is one more way these storms are not alike. A hurricane can last for a week or more as it slowly crosses the sea. Experts can often track it for days before it reaches land. A tornado may last just a few minutes, and it can show up with very little warning.

Both storms show us how strong nature can be. Thanks to weather experts, people today get better warnings than ever before. Knowing how hurricanes and tornadoes are alike and how they are not helps each family make a plan and stay safe when a big storm comes.

sessions.title: Butterflies and Moths
paragraphs: Butterflies and moths are close cousins in the insect world. Both belong to the same big group of insects, and there are many more kinds of moths than butterflies. Even though they are related, there are a few ways to tell them apart.

Butterflies and moths share the same life cycle. Each one starts as a tiny egg, then hatches into a hungry caterpillar that munches on leaves. Next it rests as a pupa while its body changes. At last it comes out as a grown insect with wings covered in tiny scales.

One difference is the time of day they are busy. Most butterflies fly during the day, when the sun is out. Most moths fly at night. That is why you might see moths flutter around a porch light after dark while butterflies rest out of sight.

Their feelers are another clue. A butterfly's feelers, called antennae, are thin with a little knob at the end, like a tiny club. A moth's feelers are often fuzzy like feathers, or they come to a point with no knob. This is one of the best ways to tell which insect you have found.

The way they rest is different, too. Lots of butterflies fold their wings straight up over their backs when they land. Lots of moths rest with their wings spread flat or folded like a tent. Moths also tend to have plump, fuzzy bodies, while butterflies are most often slim.

Last of all, they make different shells before they change. A butterfly forms a hard, smooth case called a chrysalis. Lots of moth caterpillars spin a soft silk cocoon around themselves. Although they are alike in many ways, these small differences help scientists sort them into two groups.

sessions.title: Bridges and Tunnels
paragraphs: Bridges and tunnels are two clever ways that people solve the same problem. Sometimes a road or a train track must cross something in its way, such as a river, a bay, or a mountain. Builders can choose to put a bridge over it or dig a tunnel through it.

Bridges and tunnels have a lot in common. Both help cars, trains, bikes, and people travel more quickly from place to place. Both must be planned with care by engineers. They use math and science to make sure the work is strong and safe. Both can take years to build.

The main difference is where they go. A bridge goes over the problem, so people crossing it are out in the open air. A tunnel goes under or through it, so people inside are closed in by rock, soil, or water. On a bridge you might enjoy the view, but in a tunnel you see only lights.

They are also built in very different ways. To build a bridge, workers set strong posts into the ground and join them with beams, arches, or cables. To build a tunnel, workers dig through the earth. Some use giant drills that grind slowly through rock while crews line the walls behind them.

Each one has its own challenges. Bridges must stand up to strong winds and heavy traffic. Tunnels must hold back the weight of the ground above them and keep water from leaking in. Long tunnels also need large fans to bring fresh air to the drivers inside.

Some places use both. In Virginia, the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel carries cars across the water on bridges. Then the road dips below the water through tunnels so big ships can pass. It shows how builders can join two different ideas to solve one problem.

sessions.title: Owls and Hawks
paragraphs: Owls and hawks are both birds of prey, which means they hunt other animals for food. They are among the most skilled hunters in the sky. Both play an important role in nature by keeping the number of mice and other small animals in balance.

These two kinds of birds share several tools that make them fine hunters. Both have sharp, curved talons on their feet for grabbing their food. Both have hooked beaks that help them eat. Both also have amazing eyesight that lets them spot tiny animals from far away.

However, owls and hawks hunt at different times. Most hawks hunt during the day, soaring high above fields and roadsides as they search for a meal. Most owls hunt at night. Their large eyes gather even dim light, so they can see in the dark far better than people can.

Their senses work differently, too. An owl depends heavily on its hearing. In some kinds of owls, one ear sits a little higher than the other. This helps the owl figure out exactly where a sound is coming from, even under snow. Hawks rely mainly on their sharp eyes instead.

Another difference is the way they fly. Owls have soft, fringed edges on their feathers that let them fly almost silently, so the animals below do not hear them coming. Hawks are not as quiet, but many can glide on rising warm air for a long time without flapping.

Their faces also look different. An owl has a flat, round face with both eyes pointing forward, and it can turn its head much farther than we can. A hawk has a narrower head. Although they share the same job, one works the day shift and the other works the night shift.

stops.lookFor: A similarity; 'share' and 'both' show they both have talons, hooked beaks, and sharp eyesight.

questions.a: Both are birds of prey with sharp talons, hooked beaks, and excellent eyesight, and both help keep small-animal numbers in balance.

questions.q: Name two ways they are different.

questions.a: They do the same job (hunting small animals) but at different times: hawks by day, owls by night.

sessions.title: Coral Reefs and Rainforests
paragraphs: Coral reefs and rainforests may seem like opposites, since one is under the sea and the other is on land. Yet scientists often compare them, because both are home to a huge number of living things. Coral reefs are even called the rainforests of the sea.

Both places are packed with life. A rainforest holds a vast mix of plants, insects, birds, and other animals. Many of them live nowhere else. A reef is crowded, too, with bright fish, sea turtles, crabs, and sponges. Both cover a small part of the planet, yet each holds a large share of its life.

These two places also face the same kinds of dangers. Forests can be harmed when too many trees are cut down, and reefs can be harmed when ocean water grows too warm. Because of this, people around the world are working hard to protect both of them.

However, the builders of each place are very different. In a rainforest, tall trees form the main frame, and their leaves make a thick roof called the canopy. On a reef, the builders are tiny animals called coral polyps. Over many years, their hard skeletons slowly pile up into large reefs.

The two homes are also different in how creatures find food and shelter. In the forest, monkeys and birds live in layers, from the dark floor to the sunny treetops. On a reef, fish hide in cracks and holes in the coral. Many feed on tiny living things that drift by.

Last of all, they are found in different places. Tropical rainforests grow near the equator, where rain falls almost every day. Most coral reefs grow in warm, clear, shallow seas. In the end, one is green and leafy while the other is underwater. Yet both are treasures worth caring for.

questions.a: Like rainforests, reefs are home to a huge number of different living things.

sessions.title: Jupiter and Saturn
paragraphs: Jupiter and Saturn are the two largest planets in our solar system, and they are next-door neighbors. Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun, and Saturn is the sixth. Because they share so many traits, scientists often study these two giants side by side.

Both planets are gas giants. Unlike Earth, they have no solid ground to stand on. They are made mostly of hydrogen and helium, the same gases that make up most of the Sun. Both also spin very fast, so a day on either planet lasts only about ten or eleven hours.

Both planets also have lots of moons. Scientists have found close to a hundred moons circling Jupiter and more than two hundred around Saturn. Jupiter has the largest moon in the solar system, called Ganymede. Saturn has Titan, a moon with a thick, hazy sky.

However, their rings look very different. Saturn's rings are wide and bright, and they are easy to see through a small telescope. Jupiter has rings too, but they are thin, faint, and made of dust. In fact, no one knew about them until a spacecraft flew past the planet in 1979.

Their size and weight are not the same, either. Jupiter is the bigger of the two, and it has more mass than all the other planets put together. Saturn is a bit smaller. It is so light for its size that it would float in water, if you had a tub big enough to hold it.

The weather on each planet is different, too. Jupiter has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot, which is wider than Earth and has been swirling for hundreds of years. Saturn has a strange six-sided cloud pattern at its north pole. Studying both helps scientists learn how giant planets form and change.

sessions.title: Busy Honeybees
paragraphs: Honeybees are small insects. They live and work together. A honeybee has six legs. It has four thin wings. It also has five eyes! Two big eyes are on the sides of its head. Three small eyes are on top. Its body is fuzzy. The fuzz helps it hold pollen.

Honeybees live in a home called a hive. A hive can hold thousands of bees. Each hive has one queen bee. The queen lays the eggs. Worker bees do the other jobs. They clean the hive. They feed the baby bees. They keep the hive safe, too.

Honeybees make honey. First, they fly to flowers. They drink a sweet juice called nectar. They bring it back to the hive. Then they fan it with their wings. The nectar gets thick. It turns into honey! The bees keep the honey in wax cells. Each cell has six sides.

Bees can tell each other things in a fun way. They dance! A bee finds good flowers. Then it goes home. It wiggles and turns in a path. The dance shows the other bees where to go. Then they all fly off to find the flowers.

Honeybees help us, too. When they visit flowers, pollen sticks to them. They take it from plant to plant. This helps plants make fruit and seeds. We get apples and berries thanks to bees. So the next time you see a bee, let it buzz by.

sessions.title: Penguins on Land and Sea
paragraphs: Penguins are birds, but they can not fly! A penguin has a round body. Its back is black and its belly is white. It has short legs and webbed feet, so it walks with a funny waddle. Its wings are stiff and flat. They are called flippers.

Penguins are great swimmers. They use their flippers like paddles, and their feet help them steer. Some penguins can dive very deep. They can hold their breath for a long time. In the water, they are fast and smooth. On land, they are slow and wobbly.

Penguins eat food from the sea. They catch fish with their beaks, and they eat squid, too. Some eat tiny sea animals called krill. Krill look like little shrimp. A penguin gulps its food whole because it has no teeth to chew!

Most penguins live in the southern half of the world. Some live on ice near the South Pole. Others live on warm, sandy beaches. Penguins in the cold have thick, oily feathers. They also have a layer of fat under the skin. This helps keep them warm.

Penguins live together in big groups. A group can have thousands of birds. Penguin moms and dads take turns with the egg. One stays to keep the egg warm, and the other goes to the sea to eat. Then they swap. At last, the chick hatches. It is soft and fuzzy.

sessions.title: Our Moon
paragraphs: The Moon is a big ball of rock. It travels around Earth. It takes about a month to go all the way around. The Moon is much smaller than Earth. You could line up almost four Moons across Earth! It is our closest neighbor in space.

The Moon looks bright at night. But it does not make its own light. The Sun shines on it, and the light bounces off the Moon. Then it travels to us. That is why we can see the Moon glow. It is like a giant mirror up in the night sky.

The Moon seems to change shape. Some nights it looks round and full. Other nights it looks like a skinny smile. Each night, we see a different part of its sunny side. These shapes are called phases. They start over every month.

The Moon has no air. It has no rain or wind. The ground is gray and dusty. It is covered with holes called craters. Space rocks crashed into the Moon long ago and made the holes. With no wind, the craters stay for a very long time.

People have visited the Moon! Astronauts first walked there in 1969. They left footprints in the dust, and those prints are still there today. On the Moon, you would feel very light. You could jump much higher than on Earth. What fun that would be!

sessions.title: The Amazing Octopus
paragraphs: An octopus is a sea animal with a soft body and eight long arms. It has no bones at all. This means it can squeeze through tiny cracks and holes. An octopus has a round head and two big eyes. It also has a hard beak, a bit like a bird's.

The arms of an octopus are covered with round suckers. The suckers grip rocks and grab food. They can also taste and feel things! An octopus can even grow back an arm if it loses one. It uses its arms to crawl along the sea floor.

Inside, an octopus is very different from us. It has three hearts instead of one. Its blood is blue, not red. Two of the hearts pump blood to its gills. The gills help the octopus breathe under the water.

An octopus has clever ways to stay safe. It can change the color of its skin in a blink. It can match rocks, sand, or plants. If a big fish swims close, it can squirt a cloud of dark ink. Then it zooms away and hides.

Octopuses are some of the smartest animals in the sea. Some can solve puzzles. Some have learned to open jars to get a snack inside. Scientists have seen octopuses carry shells around. They use the shells as little homes to hide in.

Octopuses live in oceans all over the world. Some live in warm, shallow water near reefs. Others live in deep, cold water. Most octopuses live alone in dens. A den might be a cave, a crack, or a pile of rocks.

sessions.title: What Is a Volcano?
paragraphs: A volcano is an opening in the ground where hot melted rock comes out. Deep under the ground, it is very hot. The heat melts rock into a thick, gooey mix. This melted rock is called magma. When it comes out of the ground, it gets a new name. Then it is called lava.

Volcanoes come in many shapes. Some are tall mountains with steep sides and a hole at the top. Others are wide and flat, like a shield lying on the ground. Some are hidden under the sea. You can not even see them!

Not all volcanoes blow up in the same way. Some burst with a big blast. They shoot ash and rocks high into the sky. Others ooze lava slowly. The lava flows down the sides like a hot, glowing river. Then it cools and turns into hard, black rock.

Volcanoes can build new land. When lava cools in the sea, it piles up. After many years, the pile can rise above the water. That is how the islands of Hawaii were made. Some of the volcanoes there are still adding land today.

Volcanoes help plants grow, too. Ash from a volcano breaks down into soil. This soil has lots of things plants need. Farmers near some volcanoes grow lots of fruit and grain. Grapes and other crops grow well there.

Scientists who study volcanoes watch them closely. They look for signs that one might blow. They check if the ground shakes or swells. They also check the gases that come out. Their work helps keep people safe.

sessions.title: The Game of Soccer
paragraphs: Soccer is the most popular sport in the world. Two teams try to kick a ball into the other team's goal. Each goal counts as one point. The team with the most goals at the end wins. It is a game of running, kicking, and teamwork.

A soccer field is a long patch of grass with white lines on it. There is a goal at each end. A goal is a big frame with a net in the back. In the middle of the field is a circle. The game starts with a kick from the center.

Each team has eleven players on the field. One player on each team is the goalie. The goalie guards the net. This is the only player who may use their hands, and only near their own goal. The others must use their feet, legs, chest, or head.

Players need many skills to play soccer well. They dribble, which means they tap the ball with their feet as they run. They pass the ball to teammates. They also shoot at the goal. Good players can do all of this while running fast.

Soccer does not need much gear. Players wear shoes with small bumps on the bottom called cleats. Cleats help them grip the grass. Many players also wear shin guards under their socks. These pads keep their legs safe from kicks.

People play soccer in almost every country. In many places, it is called football. Every four years, teams from around the world meet for a big contest called the World Cup. Millions of fans cheer for their team.

sessions.title: The Tyrant Lizard King
paragraphs: Tyrannosaurus rex was one of the biggest meat-eating dinosaurs that ever lived. Its name means tyrant lizard king. Many people call it T-rex for short. It lived about sixty-six million years ago. Its home was in what is now the western part of North America.

A T-rex was about as long as a school bus. It stood on two huge, strong back legs. Its long, heavy tail stuck straight out behind it. The tail helped it keep its balance as it walked. Its head was about as long as a grown-up is tall.

One famous thing about T-rex is its tiny arms. Each arm was about as long as a grown-up's arm. That is small for such a giant! Each hand had just two fingers. Scientists are still not sure how T-rex used its arms.

T-rex had a mouth full of sharp teeth. Some of its teeth, with the root, were longer than a banana. It also had one of the strongest bites of any land animal ever. When a tooth fell out, a new one grew in. It took the old tooth's place.

This dinosaur also had strong senses. Scientists have studied the inside of its skull. The part of the brain used for smell was very large. This tells them T-rex had a great sense of smell. Its eyes faced forward. This may have helped it judge how far away things were.

Today, we learn about T-rex from fossils. Fossils are bones and other remains that turned to stone over time. One of the most complete T-rex skeletons was found in South Dakota. Museums show fossils like this. They help people see how big this dinosaur really was.

sessions.title: All About Pizza
paragraphs: Pizza is a flat, round bread baked with tasty toppings on top. It is one of the most loved foods in the world. People eat it at parties, at home, and at school. A pizza has three main parts: the crust, the sauce, and the cheese.

The crust is the bottom layer of a pizza. It is made from dough. Dough is a mix of flour, water, salt, and yeast. Yeast is made of tiny living things that make the dough puff up. Some crusts are thin and crunchy. Others are thick and soft, like a pillow.

Next comes the sauce. Most pizza sauce is made from tomatoes. Cooks often add garlic, salt, and herbs such as basil. The sauce is spread over the dough with a spoon. Some pizzas use other sauces instead, such as a white cheese sauce.

Cheese goes on top of the sauce. The most common pizza cheese is mozzarella. It melts into a soft, stretchy layer. That is why you see long strings of cheese when you pull a slice away! Many people also add toppings, such as peppers, mushrooms, or olives.

Pizza must bake in a very hot oven. Some pizza ovens are made of brick and heated by a wood fire. These ovens get much hotter than an oven in a kitchen at home. In a hot brick oven, a pizza can cook in just a minute or two.

Pizza first became popular in Naples, a city in Italy. People there have made it for hundreds of years. Later, Italian families brought pizza to other countries. Today, cooks around the world make their own kinds. Each place adds its own special toppings.

sessions.title: Firefighters Help Us
paragraphs: Firefighters are helpers who work to keep us safe. Their best-known job is putting out fires. But they do lots of other jobs, too. They help people who are hurt or stuck. They also give first aid. Some get paid for this work, and some help for free.

Firefighters work out of a fire station. Many of them stay there for a whole day and night at a time. The station has beds, a kitchen, and a big garage. When the alarm rings, the crew gets ready fast. They jump on their trucks and go.

The gear they wear keeps them safe from heat and smoke. They wear a helmet, a thick coat, and heavy pants. They also wear boots and gloves. On their back, they carry a tank of air. A mask lets them breathe clean air in a smoky house.

Fire trucks carry the tools the crew needs. Some trucks have tall ladders that can reach high windows. Others carry long hoses and tanks of water. The crew can also hook a hose to a fire hydrant on the street. The hydrant is linked to water pipes under the ground.

Firefighters also teach people how to stay safe. They visit schools to share safety tips. For example, they tell kids to stop, drop, and roll if their clothes catch fire. They also tell families to test their smoke alarms. Each family should pick a spot to meet outside.

This job takes a lot of hard work. The crew trains often to stay strong and ready. They practice climbing ladders and carrying heavy tools. They also keep learning first aid. All of this helps them be ready when someone needs help.

sessions.title: Saturn, the Ringed Planet
paragraphs: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun. It is the second largest planet in our solar system. Only Jupiter is bigger. Saturn is so large that more than seven hundred Earths could fit inside it. Many people think it is the prettiest planet because of its bright rings.

Saturn is very different from Earth. It does not have solid ground to stand on. It is made mostly of two gases called hydrogen and helium. Deep inside, these gases are squeezed into a thick liquid. Saturn is so light for its size that it would float in a giant tub of water!

The rings of Saturn are its most famous feature. From far away, they look like smooth, flat bands. Up close, they are made of chunks of ice and rock. Some are as tiny as grains of sand. Others are as big as a house. The rings are very wide but very thin.

Saturn also has a huge family of moons. In fact, it has more known moons than any other planet. Its largest moon is called Titan. Titan is bigger than the planet Mercury, and it has a thick, hazy sky. Another moon sprays jets of icy water out into space.

Time works differently on Saturn. The planet spins very fast, so one day there lasts only about ten and a half hours. But Saturn is far from the Sun, so its trip around the Sun takes a long time. One year on Saturn is about twenty-nine years on Earth.

Scientists have learned a lot about Saturn from spacecraft. One spacecraft circled Saturn for about thirteen years. It took amazing pictures of the rings and moons. It even sent a probe down to land on Titan. Thanks to trips like this, we know more about this ringed giant.

sessions.title: Cities Under the Sea
paragraphs: A coral reef is a large shape under the sea. It is built by tiny sea animals called corals. Reefs are found in warm, clear, shallow water. They are often called the rainforests of the sea because so many kinds of life live there. Reefs come in amazing shapes and colors.

Corals can look like rocks or plants, but they are animals. Each coral is made of many small, soft living things called polyps. A polyp has a body shaped like a tube. It has a ring of tiny arms around its mouth. Polyps build hard, stony cups around themselves to stay safe.

Corals have a special team partner. Tiny living things called algae live inside the coral's body. The algae use sunlight to make food, and they share that food with the coral. In return, the coral gives the algae a safe home. The algae also give many corals their bright colors.

Reefs grow very slowly. New polyps build on top of old ones, layer after layer. Over thousands of years, these layers form a giant reef. The largest group of reefs in the world is the Great Barrier Reef, near Australia. It is so big that it can be seen from space.

Coral reefs are home to a huge number of sea creatures. Bright fish dart in and out of cracks. Sea turtles, crabs, and sea stars live there. Some fish, such as clownfish, hide in the waving arms of sea anemones. Reefs give these animals food and places to rest.

Coral reefs need care to stay healthy. When the water gets too warm, corals can lose their algae and turn white. People can help by keeping beaches clean and using less plastic. Scientists also grow young corals and plant them on reefs to help them grow back.

questions.a: Because so many kinds of life live there.

sessions.title: Inside the Piano
paragraphs: The piano is a musical instrument that people have played for more than three hundred years. It was invented in Italy around the year 1700. Today, pianos are heard in homes, schools, and concert halls all around the world. Let us see how this amazing instrument works.

A standard piano has eighty-eight keys. Fifty-two of them are white, and thirty-six are black. The keys on the left side play low notes that sound deep and rumbly. The keys on the right side play high notes that sound bright. The black keys come in twos and threes.

A piano makes sound in an interesting way. Inside the piano are many tight metal strings. When you press a key, a small hammer covered in felt swings up and hits a string. The string shakes very fast, and this shaking makes a sound. When you let go, a soft pad stops the string.

Most pianos also have pedals near the floor. A player presses them with their feet. The pedal on the right lets the notes keep ringing after the keys are let go. The pedal on the left makes the sound softer. These pedals help players add feeling to their music.

Pianos come in two main types. A grand piano is long and wide, and its strings lie flat inside. Its lid can open up like a wing. An upright piano is tall and narrow, with its strings standing up and down. Upright pianos fit well in smaller rooms, such as a living room.

Learning to play the piano takes patience and practice. Beginners often start with simple songs that use just a few keys. Over time, they learn to read music and play with both hands at once. Many people also play electric keyboards, which copy the sound of a real piano.

questions.a: Pressing a key makes a felt hammer hit a metal string, and the string shakes to make sound.

questions.a: Any two: the keys, how it makes sound, the pedals, the two types, learning to play.

sessions.title: Hurricanes: Giant Spinning Storms
paragraphs: A hurricane is a huge, spinning storm that forms over warm ocean water. These storms bring strong winds, heavy rain, and high waves. A hurricane can be hundreds of miles wide. From space, it looks like a giant swirl of white clouds. In some parts of the world, the same kind of storm is called a typhoon or a cyclone.

A hurricane needs a few things to form. First, the sea water must be warm, usually at least eighty degrees. Warm, wet air rises from the sea and cools as it goes up. This makes tall clouds. More air rushes in to take its place. Because of the way Earth turns, the whole storm begins to spin.

A hurricane has several parts. In the very middle is the eye, a calm spot where the sky can even look clear. Around the eye is the eyewall. It is a ring of tall clouds with the strongest winds and the heaviest rain. Long bands of clouds and rain spiral out from the center like the arms of a pinwheel.

Weather experts keep a close watch on these storms. They use satellites in space to take pictures of storms from above. Special planes, sometimes called hurricane hunters, even fly right into the storm to gather facts. All of this helps experts guess where a storm will go and how strong it will get.

Since experts can track storms days ahead of time, towns have time to get ready. Families can pack things such as water, flashlights, and batteries. Towns share safety plans and tell people when to move to a safer place. In the Atlantic Ocean, hurricane season runs from June through November each year.

stops.question: What is this first paragraph mostly about?
stops.lookFor: It defines a hurricane: a huge spinning storm over warm ocean water, and other names for it.

stops.question: How does this paragraph connect to the main topic of hurricanes?

questions.a: Hurricanes.

questions.a: How they form, their parts, how experts track them, and how people get ready.

questions.a: The calm area in the very middle of the storm, where the sky can even look clear.

sessions.title: How a Cactus Survives
paragraphs: A cactus is a plant that is built to live in hot, dry places such as deserts. Almost all wild cactuses grow in North and South America. They come in many shapes and sizes. Some are tiny round balls that fit in your hand, and some are giants taller than a house. Even though they look different, they all share some clever tricks.

The most useful part of a cactus is its thick stem. The stem works like a water tank. When it rains, the cactus soaks up as much water as it can and stores it inside. Many cactuses have folds on the stem. The folds let the stem swell up when it fills with water, then shrink as the water gets used.

Most cactuses do not have flat green leaves. Instead, they have sharp spines, which are a special kind of leaf. Spines keep away animals that want to eat the plant. They also shade the plant from the hot sun. A cactus has a waxy skin, too, which keeps water from drying up into the air.

One of the most famous cactuses is the saguaro. It grows in a desert in Arizona and Mexico. A saguaro can grow taller than forty feet and live for more than one hundred years. It grows very slowly, and it may not grow its first arm for many years. In late spring, it blooms with white flowers.

Cactuses are also a big help to desert animals. Birds such as woodpeckers carve out holes in saguaros to make nests. Bats and bees sip nectar from cactus flowers. Many animals eat cactus fruit, which is often sweet and juicy. In this way, one cactus can give food and shelter to many creatures.

stops.question: What is this first paragraph mostly about?
stops.lookFor: It introduces cactuses: plants built to survive in hot, dry places, with many shapes but shared features.

stops.lookFor: The stem stores water, which is one of the clever features that help a cactus survive in dry places.

questions.q: How do cactuses help desert animals?
questions.a: They give food like nectar and fruit, and shelter like nest holes for birds.

sessions.title: A Home in Space
paragraphs: The International Space Station is a giant science lab that circles Earth high above our heads. With its huge solar panels, it is about the size of a football field. People have lived and worked on board without a break since the year 2000. Many countries worked together to build it.

The space station moves very fast, at about seventeen thousand miles per hour. At that speed, it goes around the whole planet about every ninety minutes. This means the crew can see about sixteen sunrises every single day. The station flies about two hundred fifty miles above the ground.

Life on the station is very different from life on Earth. People and things float around inside. The crew sleeps in small sleeping bags tied to the walls so they do not drift away. They drink from pouches with straws. To move from place to place, they hold onto rails and push off gently.

Staying healthy in space takes extra work. When the body floats all the time, muscles and bones can grow weak. To stay strong, the crew works out for about two hours each day. They use special machines. One is a treadmill with straps that hold them down, and another is a bike with no seat.

The main job of the space station is science. The crew runs hundreds of tests that can only be done in space. They grow plants to learn how food might be grown on long trips. On a clear night, you can sometimes see the station from your own backyard. It looks like a bright dot of light moving quickly across the sky.

sessions.title: Triceratops, the Three-Horned Face
paragraphs: Triceratops was a large dinosaur that ate plants. It lived about sixty-eight to sixty-six million years ago in what is now the western part of North America. Its name means three-horned face, which describes its most famous feature very well. It shared its home with many other dinosaurs, including the mighty T-rex.

The head of this dinosaur was one of the largest heads of any land animal that has ever lived. Above each eye stood a horn that could grow about three feet long. A shorter horn sat on top of its nose. Behind its head was a wide, bony shield called a frill, which spread out like a fan.

Scientists have several ideas about why it had horns and a frill. The horns may have helped it guard itself or push back against rivals of its own kind. The frill may have helped animals of the same kind know each other, much like a flag. These parts may have had more than one use.

Its body was built like a heavy tank, with four sturdy legs holding up its thick body. A grown one could reach about thirty feet long and weigh more than an elephant. Instead of front teeth, it had a sharp beak, a bit like a parrot's. It used the beak to snip off tough leaves and stems from low plants.

People who dig for fossils have found many Triceratops skulls in places such as Montana and South Dakota. Since so many have been found, it is one of the best-studied dinosaurs of all. Each new find adds another clue to the story of how this great creature lived long ago.

stops.question: What is this first paragraph mostly about?
stops.lookFor: It introduces Triceratops: a plant-eating dinosaur, when and where it lived, and what its name means.

stops.lookFor: It describes the horns and frill on its head, which explain why it got that name.

sessions.title: The Story of Basketball
paragraphs: Basketball is a fast team sport. Players try to score points by shooting a ball through a raised hoop. It is played by millions of people around the world, in school gyms, on outdoor courts, and in huge arenas. Unlike many other sports, basketball was invented on purpose by one person.

The game was created in 1891 by a teacher named James Naismith in Springfield, Massachusetts. He wanted to give his students an active game they could play indoors during the cold winter months. For the first hoops, he nailed two peach baskets to the railing of a gym balcony. After every basket, someone had to climb up and get the ball out.

A basketball court is a smooth, rectangular floor with a hoop at each end. Each hoop is attached to a flat backboard. It stands exactly ten feet above the floor, just as it did in the very first game. Lines painted on the court mark the edges, the center circle, and the three-point line.

Each team has five players on the court at a time. Players move the ball by dribbling, which means bouncing it with one hand while they walk or run. A player holding the ball may not run without dribbling. Doing that breaks a rule called traveling, and the other team gets the ball.

Teams can score points in several ways. A regular shot made from inside the three-point line is worth two points. A shot from behind that line is worth three points. When a player is fouled, they may get free throws. These are shots taken from a special line, and each one that goes in is worth one point.

sessions.title: Layers of the Rainforest
paragraphs: A rainforest is a thick, green forest that gets lots of rain all year. The ones called tropical rainforests grow near the middle of the Earth, where the weather stays warm all year long. They cover only a small part of the land on Earth. Even so, they are home to about half of the kinds of plants and animals in the world.

Scientists say a rainforest has layers, much like the floors of a tall building. The top layer is called the emergent layer. Here, the tops of the tallest trees poke out high above the rest. Below it is the canopy. This thick roof of leaves and branches soaks up most of the sunlight that hits the forest.

Under the canopy is the understory, a shady, damp layer where young trees and leafy plants grow. Only a little sunlight reaches this layer. Because of this, many plants here have very large leaves to catch as much light as they can. At the very bottom is the forest floor, which is dark and covered with fallen leaves.

Each layer of the forest has its own animals. Bright birds such as toucans and parrots fly through the canopy, while monkeys swing from branch to branch. Sloths hang upside down and move so slowly that tiny green plants called algae grow on their fur. Frogs, bugs, and lots of other small creatures live down near the ground.

These forests matter to people all over the world. Their plants give off the oxygen we breathe and help keep the air clean and healthy. Many foods we enjoy, such as bananas, chocolate, and vanilla, first came from plants that grow there. Because these forests are so important, many people are working hard to protect them.

stops.lookFor: It introduces rainforests: lots of rain, warm weather near the equator, and home to about half of all kinds of plants and animals.

stops.question: How does this paragraph connect to the one before it?
stops.lookFor: Both describe the layers of the rainforest; the one before tells the top two layers and this one tells the bottom two.

questions.a: Rainforests.
